property_summary: For any caller and any single call to play with exactly TICKET_AMOUNT wei, the reference contract always resets pot to 0 when the computed random equals 0 (i.e. pot == 0 after the call whenever random==0); the mutant flips the branch and will leave pot nonzero for some inputs (when random==0) causing pot to differ.

For any caller paying exactly the ticket amount, the reference contract either leaves pot unchanged (if no win) or resets pot to 0 after a winning play; the mutant flips which random outcome is winning, so there exist inputs where pot is not reset to 0 in the mutant while it is in the reference.

For any caller paying exactly the ticket amount, after play() completes the reference contract leaves pot equal to 0 whenever the derived random == 0; the mutant flips the winning condition to random == 1 so there exist fuzzed block timestamps that make random==0 and thus the mutant fails to reset pot to 0 while the reference does.

For any caller paying the exact ticket amount, if the derived on-chain randomness yields 0 then the reference contract always resets pot to 0 after play() (pays out), but the mutant flips the win condition to random==1 and therefore for some block timestamp/difficulty inputs the mutant will leave pot nonzero while the reference sets it to zero.

For any caller who pays the exact ticket amount and when block.timestamp and block.difficulty produce random == 0, the reference contract always resets pot to 0 after play() completes; the mutant flips the winning condition to random == 1, so for some timestamp/difficulty the mutant will leave pot nonzero while the reference sets it to zero.

For any caller sending exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play, the reference contract always resets pot to 0 whenever the generated random == 0 (i.e. when the winner branch executes), whereas the mutant inverts the condition and therefore can leave pot non-zero for that same random value, causing divergence.

For any caller who sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play, the reference contract either leaves pot > 0 when no payout occurs or resets pot to 0 whenever it makes a payout to the caller and fee to bank; the mutant inverts the condition so there exist inputs (a caller and the block state that produce random == 0) where the reference resets pot to 0 but the mutant leaves pot nonzero, breaking the rule.

For any caller who sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play, the reference contract always sets pot to 0 when the pseudo-random value computed inside play equals 0; the mutant inverts the condition so there exist block states (timestamp/difficulty) that make random == 0 where the reference sets pot to 0 but the mutant leaves pot nonzero, so pot==0 always after play for those block states in the reference but not in the mutant.

For any caller who sends exactly the ticket amount, whenever the reference contract results in pot == 0 immediately after play(), the mutant may leave pot != 0 for the same inputs; equivalently, for all admissible fuzzed callers and block timestamps, if play() on the reference yields pot == 0 then pot == 0 holds (the reference always resets pot when it pays), but the mutant fails this for some inputs.

For every admissible caller who sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play(), if the pseudo-random value computed inside play() equals 0 then the reference contract always resets pot to 0 after play(); the mutant that inverts the condition leaves pot nonzero for some inputs (so pot==0 no longer holds universally).

For every call to play() that pays the exact ticket amount and results in a winning branch (random == 0), the reference contract resets pot to 0 after paying the fee and winner; the mutant that omits the reset can leave pot > 0 after such a winning play.

After any call to play() that sends the correct ticket amount, the reference contract always leaves pot equal to 0 (because it pays out and resets pot), whereas the mutant that omits the pot reset can leave pot > 0 for some sequence of plays — so for every admissible single-play input the reference guarantees pot == 0 afterwards, and the mutant can violate this.

For any single successful play() call that pays the exact ticket amount and results in a win (the contract sends payouts and fee), the reference C always resets pot to 0 after the call; the mutant that omits the reset can leave pot > 0 for some winning calls, so pot == 0 is a universal postcondition the reference satisfies but the mutant can violate.

If a caller pays exactly the ticket amount and the contract's pot before the call is non-zero, then whenever the play() call results in a payout (random==0) the reference contract's pot after the call equals 0, but the mutant that omits resetting pot can leave pot > 0 for some such inputs (same caller, nonzero initial pot).

For any caller and any starting pot value, if a play() call is made paying the exact ticket amount and the call does NOT take the winning branch (random != 0), then the pot after the call equals the previous pot plus the ticket amount; the mutant can violate this because removing the pot reset only affects winning branch, so we instead observe that on losing branch both versions must behave identically — but because randomness depends on block values we can fuzz block.timestamp to force losing branch and detect divergence in subsequent call sequences where the mutant's lingering pot causes later losing-branch behavior to differ.

For any caller sending exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play, the reference always leaves pot nonzero only when the caller loses (random==1) and otherwise resets pot to 0 only when paying out; the mutant however always resets pot to 0 at the end, so there exist inputs (a winning payout path where random==1 is false for mutant's extra reset) that make pot differ — specifically: after a play call with correct ticket payment, the reference's pot equals 0 iff the contract paid out that round, whereas the mutant always sets pot to 0; thus the general rule is that after play, pot is zero only when random==0 (payout happened), which the mutant violates for some inputs.

For any caller who sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play, C ensures that pot == 0 iff the round paid out (i.e. when random == 0); the mutant sets pot = 0 unconditionally at the end, so there exist inputs where C leaves pot nonzero but the mutant forces it to zero.

For every valid play call (msg.value == 10) the reference contract leaves pot equal to 0 exactly when that round paid out (random == 0), i.e. after play pot is 0 only if a payout occurred; the mutant unconditionally zeroes pot at the end, so there exist inputs where the reference leaves pot non-zero but the mutant forces it to 0.

For any caller sending the exact ticket amount to play, the reference contract leaves pot == 0 after play if and only if the round paid out (random == 0); the mutant unconditionally sets pot = 0 at the end, so there exist inputs where the reference leaves pot > 0 but the mutant forces pot == 0.

For every valid play call (msg.value == 10) the reference contract leaves pot == 0 exactly when the round paid out (random == 0), so after play pot is nonzero for some inputs (when random == 1) — the mutant unconditionally zeroes pot at end, breaking that property for those inputs.

For any caller and any valid ticket payment, the reference contract always increases pot by the ticket amount after play (so pot new = old pot + TICKET_AMOUNT) but the mutated version can leave pot as 0 when the caller wins (breaking that invariant).

For any call to play() that provides the exact ticket payment, the reference contract always increases pot by TICKET_AMOUNT (except when pot reset after paying a winner, the post-call pot equals either previous pot + TICKET_AMOUNT or 0 depending on randomness) — the mutant that moves pot increment after randomness can produce a pot of 0 when the caller wins even though the caller paid the ticket, violating the invariant that pot after a losing call equals previous pot + TICKET_AMOUNT; we assert that if the caller does NOT win (i.e., play does not reset pot to 0) then pot increased by TICKET_AMOUNT, which holds for the reference for all admissible inputs but is broken by the mutant for some inputs.

For any caller that pays the exact ticket amount and for any starting pot, after play() returns either the pot becomes 0 (the caller won) or the pot increases by the ticket amount (the caller lost) — the mutant can produce a case where play() returns and the pot is unchanged (neither 0 nor increased by the ticket) because the increment was applied after a winner payout, violating this invariant.

For any caller who pays the exact ticket amount, after play() returns the pot is either reset to 0 (the caller won) or increased by exactly TICKET_AMOUNT (the caller lost); the mutant that moves the pot increment after the win-check can produce a post-call pot of 0 even when it should have increased, violating this rule.

For any caller that sends exactly the ticket amount to play(), if the play() call does not reset pot to 0 (i.e. the caller did not win) then the pot after the call equals the pot before the call plus TICKET_AMOUNT; the mutant that moves the pot increment after the win-check can leave pot unchanged for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller sending exactly the ticket amount, the reference contract always either (a) transfers the fee to bank and resets pot to 0 when the random outcome equals 0, or (b) leaves the pot increased by the ticket amount when outcome != 0; specifically, because reference uses modulus 2 the chance of leaving pot unchanged equals 1/2 for every call—changing modulus to 3 reduces win probability and therefore there exist inputs (i.e. fuzzed block.timestamp) where the mutant results in a different pot value than the reference (the test asserts that after a play the pot is either unchanged or zero, which the reference always obeys for all admissible inputs while the mutant can violate this because its win probability differs).

For any caller sending exactly the ticket amount, after calling play the contract's pot is either reset to 0 (if the caller 'wins') or increased by exactly TICKET_AMOUNT (if the caller doesn't win); changing modulus from 2 to 3 makes the win probability different but does not violate this invariant for the reference — the mutant can cause inputs (block.timestamp/block.difficulty) where the pot is neither 0 nor increased by exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, so the single-run observable postcondition can differ.

For any caller that sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT and any block state, after play() completes the contract's pot is either 0 (the caller won) or increased by exactly TICKET_AMOUNT (the caller did not win); changing the randomness modulus to 3 makes there exist block inputs where the mutant leaves pot unchanged when reference would have paid out (violating the rule).

For any caller that sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, after play() completes the contract's pot is either 0 (the call hit the winning branch) or increased by exactly TICKET_AMOUNT (the call did not win); changing the randomness modulus to 3 makes some block inputs where the mutant's randomness outcome differs and thus can leave pot in a state that violates this postcondition for the same fuzzed inputs.

For any caller who sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, after play() the contract's pot is either 0 (the caller won and payout occurred) or increased by exactly TICKET_AMOUNT (the caller didn't win); changing the randomness modulus to 3 makes there exist block states where the mutant's randomness outcome differs and thus this postcondition can be violated for some fuzzed block.timestamp/block.difficulty, so the property distinguishes the mutant.

For any caller who pays exactly TICKET_AMOUNT into play, after the call the contract's pot is either increased by that amount (if caller loses) or reset to zero (if caller wins) and the contract's bank should never receive less than FEE_AMOUNT when a win occurs; the mutant that pays the fee to the winner can leave the bank with less than FEE_AMOUNT, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller who pays exactly the ticket amount and triggers play, if play results in draining the pot (pot becomes 0) then the bank's balance must have increased by at least FEE_AMOUNT; the mutant that transfers the fee to msg.sender can leave the bank with less than FEE_AMOUNT for some inputs.

For any caller paying the ticket and causing the game to drain the pot (pot becomes 0), the bank's balance must increase by exactly FEE_AMOUNT (the fee is always sent to bank); the mutant that sends the fee to msg.sender will sometimes leave bank's balance unchanged, violating this rule.

For any caller who pays exactly TICKET_AMOUNT and after a play that drains the pot (pot == 0), the total ETH held by contract C plus the bank's balance equals the prior total ETH (conservation of ETH between contract and bank when pot is drained); the mutant that redirects the fee to msg.sender can break this conservation for some inputs because the winner may receive extra ETH that should have gone to the bank, changing the split between contract and bank compared to reference.

For any caller who pays exactly TICKET_AMOUNT and triggers play, if play drains the pot (pot becomes 0) then the bank address (the deployer) must have received FEE_AMOUNT from the contract (i.e., address(bank) balance increases by at least FEE_AMOUNT); the mutant that sends the fee to msg.sender can leave the bank without that fee for some inputs, breaking the rule.

After any call to play sending exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, if the caller wins (random==0) then the reference contract always sets pot to 0 only after paying bank the FEE_AMOUNT and paying the winner the remaining pot-FEE_AMOUNT, so the caller receipt equals previous pot+TICKET_AMOUNT-FEE_AMOUNT and pot is 0 afterwards; the mutant that zeroes pot before transfers can cause the winner to receive 0-FEE_AMOUNT (underflow prevented by checked arithmetic so effectively pays zero), thus violating the payment/pot update rule for some inputs (when the random branch triggers).

After any successful play() call that sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, the reference contract always leaves pot == 0 and transfers to the caller an amount equal to the previous pot + TICKET_AMOUNT - FEE_AMOUNT when the winning branch triggers; the mutant that zeroes pot before transfers can cause the caller to receive less (or zero) while pot is still 0, violating that the caller receives the accumulated pot minus the fee when they win.

For any caller and any initial pot value, when play() is invoked with exactly TICKET_AMOUNT and the contract's random branch makes the caller win, the reference always transfers (previous pot + TICKET_AMOUNT - FEE_AMOUNT) to the caller and leaves pot == 0; the mutant that zeroes pot before transfers can cause the caller to receive less (or zero) for some executions, so asserting the caller's balance increases by that exact amount distinguishes them.

For any caller sending exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, after play() completes the reference contract's pot is always 0 (regardless of random branch), whereas the mutant can leave pot != 0 or result in inconsistent transfers when the winning branch executes because it zeroes pot before transfers; thus the invariant pot == 0 after play() holds for the reference for every admissible input but is violated by the mutant for some inputs.

For any caller who sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play(), if the caller wins (the contract executes the winning branch) then the reference contract leaves pot == 0 after play() completes; the mutant that zeroes pot before transfers can cause the contract to revert or otherwise behave so that trying to call play() (from a contract whose receive reverts) produces a different observable outcome — therefore the reference always leaves pot == 0 after play() for all admissible inputs, while the mutant can cause play() to revert for some adversarial receiver behavior.

For any caller paying exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play, the reference contract always reduces pot to 0 whenever it pays out a winner (random==0), whereas the mutant that omits transferring the fee can leave contract balance inconsistent with pot causing pot != 0 behavior observable via address(c).balance after play; the test fuzzes the caller address to trigger the payout path and checks that after play the contract balance equals pot==0 condition (reference: balance 0 when payout occurred), which the mutant can violate for some inputs.

For any caller who sends exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play, if the contract's pot becomes zero after play then the contract's ether balance must also be zero; the mutant that omits paying the fee can make pot = 0 while leaving the contract balance > 0 for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any caller sending exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play, whenever pot becomes 0 after the call the contract's ether balance must also be 0; the mutant that skips transferring the fee can make pot = 0 while leaving contract balance > 0 for some inputs (the winner receives pot-FEE but fee not sent out, leaving leftover balance).

For any caller who pays exactly TICKET_AMOUNT to play, if after the call the contract's pot is zero then the contract's ether balance must also be zero (the reference always transfers the fee out when paying a winner, but the mutant that omits the fee transfer can leave contract balance > 0 while pot == 0).

For any caller paying exactly TICKET_AMOUNT, if after play() the contract's pot is zero then the contract's balance must also be zero (the reference always sends the FEE_AMOUNT to bank before zeroing pot); the mutant that omits sending the fee can leave contract balance > 0 while pot == 0 for some inputs.
